quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Rest your hand on the clutch and brake lever.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rest your hand on the clutch and brake lever.
questions.explanation: In risky areas like intersections, shopping centers, school zones, and construction zones, keep your hand ready on the clutch and both brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to danger.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you need to slow down quickly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you need to slow down quickly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's single brake light is not as visible as a car's two brake lights. Flash your brake light when you slow down faster than other drivers expect. This helps them notice you.

questions.question: When carrying a heavy load, what should you adjust?
questions.correctAnswerText: The suspension.
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to match the manufacturer's settings for that weight.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help prevent serious injury?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ear buds.
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high ankle boots, and durable gloves. Ear buds do not protect you from injury.

questions.question: How can you make yourself more visible to other riders and drivers?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on all the time.
Ride on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on all the time.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright and reflective clothing, keep your headlight on at all times, and change your lane position as needed based on road conditions.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Give you a good view of the shoulder.
Make it hard to see road hazards.
Let other riders share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and lets them see you. Do not stay in another driver's blind spot for long periods.

questions.question: After you start turning, what should you do with the throttle?

options.text: Keep your speed steady or speed up slowly.
Do not think about your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your speed steady or speed up slowly.
questions.explanation: Roll the throttle smoothly through a turn to keep your suspension stable. Keep your speed steady or speed up gradually through the turn.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What is the best way to ride in a group while staying close together and staying safe?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close while giving each person enough space to stay safe. Ride in a single line when going around curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side by side.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT required for good eye or face shield protection?

options.text: It must be too tight for sunglasses or eyeglasses.
It must be free of scratches.
It must let you see clearly to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: It must be too tight for sunglasses or eyeglasses.
questions.explanation: Good eye and face protection must be free of scratches, resist damage, allow clear side views, fasten securely, let air flow to prevent fogging, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: How can you tell if your rear tire has gone flat while riding?

options.text: You hear a hissing noise from the rear of the bike.
The back end jerks from side to side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end jerks from side to side.
questions.explanation: When your rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk from side to side. Riders rarely hear a tire fail.

questions.question: Motorcycle headlights are:

options.text: Usually stronger than a car's headlights.
Usually the same strength as a car's headlights.
Usually weaker than a car's headlights.
Usually larger than a car's headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually weaker than a car's headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are generally smaller and weaker than car headlights.

questions.question: For a long trip, you should:

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel drowsy.
Dress warmly to protect yourself from cold wind and rain.
Ride more than 12 hours a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to protect yourself from cold wind and rain.
questions.explanation: To reduce fatigue on a long trip, wear clothing that protects you from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day and take rest breaks at least every two hours. Do not use stimulants like caffeine, as they cause extreme fatigue when they wear off.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, they should:

options.text: Sit as far back on the seat as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when you lean.
questions.explanation: Passengers should lean when the operator leans. A passenger should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator and hold firmly onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, all of these are important except:
questions.correctAnswerText: The helmet looks attractive.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly around your head and have no visible damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections
questions.explanation: The greatest risk of conflict happens at intersections. Stay alert at intersections where another vehicle may cross in front of you.

questions.question: Riding directly next to another vehicle:

options.text: Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
Is safer than riding behind the vehicle.
Is safe because it limits your escape routes.
Should only be done during daytime.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride directly next to another vehicle because you may end up in the driver's blind spot. If the driver cannot see you, they may change lanes into you without warning. Riding next to a vehicle is also dangerous because it blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Many over-the-counter drugs:

options.text: Only affect your riding if you drink alcohol at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make riding more dangerous.
questions.explanation: Like alcohol, many drugs (including prescription medications, over-the-counter medications, and illegal drugs) can impair your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: The front brake provides what percentage of a motorcycle's braking power?
questions.correctAnswerText: 75 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 75 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Rain suits:

options.text: Should not balloon out when riding.
Are not needed because motorcycles should not be ridden in rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not balloon out when riding.
questions.explanation: Quality rain suits made for motorcycles resist tearing and ballooning when riding at high speeds.

questions.question: When riding in a group, motorcyclists should:

options.text: Make their space cushions half as large as usual.
Keep enough space around each rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep enough space around each rider.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close together but keep enough space around each rider for safety.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking alcohol, which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for your friend.
Get your friend involved in other activities to slow their drinking.
Keep your friend from leaving until they are sober.
Let your friend ride their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let your friend ride their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has been drinking to ride a motorcycle. Instead, arrange safe transportation, keep them busy with other activities, and prevent them from leaving until they are sober.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Sit as far back on the seat as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with the rider.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger, tell them to lean with you during turns and curves. They should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on the left, you should:

options.text: Stay in the right part of your lane.
Move to the left part of your lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle in front.
Not use your signal so you don't distract the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the left part of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing on the left, ride in the left part of your lane. Signal your turn, check for oncoming traffic, and pass when safe. Signal again and return to your lane when it is clear.

questions.question: To reduce injury in a crash, do all of the following except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Have a windshield.
questions.explanation: Wear an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing to reduce injury risk. A windshield is not required for safety.
